# gog 🧭 — Google Workspace from the terminal `gog` is one command-line client for Gmail, Calendar, Drive, Docs, Sheets, and the wider Google Workspace surface. It is built for people, scripts, CI, and agents that need explicit account routing, machine-readable output, and safety controls. ```bash gog --readonly gmail search 'is:unread newer_than:7d' --max 10 --json gog --readonly calendar events --today --json gog --readonly drive audit sharing --parent --json ``` For least-privilege Gmail authorization, use `gog auth add you@example.com --services gmail --gmail-scope send` for sending only, or `--gmail-scope read-send` to also read messages without mailbox-modification or settings-management permissions. ## Install Homebrew is the shortest path on macOS and Linux. Prebuilt macOS binaries require macOS 15 or later: ```bash brew install openclaw/tap/gogcli gog --version ``` With Go: ```bash go install github.com/openclaw/gogcli/cmd/gog@latest gog --version ``` Install scripts using the former `github.com/steipete/gogcli` module path should switch to `github.com/openclaw/gogcli` as shown above. Docker images, Windows archives, raw macOS/Linux binaries, and source builds are covered in the [install guide](docs/install.md). ## Quick start Create a Desktop OAuth client in a [Google Cloud project](https://console.cloud.google.com/auth/clients), download its JSON file, and authorize only the services you need: ```bash gog auth credentials set ~/Downloads/client_secret_*.json gog auth add you@gmail.com --services gmail,calendar,drive export GOG_ACCOUNT=you@gmail.com gog auth doctor --check gog gmail search 'newer_than:7d' --max 10 ``` `gog auth you@gmail.com` is shorthand for `gog auth add you@gmail.com`, with the same flags. For Gmail queries beginning with `-`, place all flags before `--`; see [Search and Read](docs/gmail-workflows.md#search-and-read). The [five-minute quickstart](docs/quickstart.md) covers API enablement, the OAuth consent screen, weekly-token-expiry avoidance, headless authorization, and account defaults. ## Work with Google services Commands follow the resource you are working with. These are the common entry points; the [examples](docs/examples.md) and generated [command index](docs/commands/README.md) cover the full surface. | Work | Start with | | --- | --- | | Mail and calendars | `gog gmail search`, `gog calendar events` | | Files and sharing | `gog drive ls`, `gog drive audit sharing` | | Docs, Sheets, Slides, and Forms | `gog docs`, `gog sheets`, `gog slides`, `gog forms` | | Contacts and tasks | `gog contacts`, `gog tasks` | | Meetings and chat | `gog meet`, `gog chat`, `gog zoom` | | Analytics and publishing | `gog analytics`, `gog searchconsole`, `gog adsense`, `gog youtube` | | Workspace administration | `gog admin`, `gog groups`, `gog keep` | | Discovery API fallback | `gog api describe`, `gog api call` | Generic API commands support service-hosted Discovery documents such as Meet v2 when the default central Directory returns 404. Explicit `GOG_DISCOVERY_BASE_URL` overrides retain their existing behavior. `GOG_GOOGLE_API_BASE_URL=http(s)://host[:port]` sends Google API requests for `https://googleapis.com` and `https://*.googleapis.com` to a test server, emulator, proxy, or relay that adds credentials outside gog. Path and query are kept and the original host is sent as `X-Forwarded-Host`. While it is set, gog attaches no credentials to Google API requests (no OAuth, ADC, service-account, `--access-token`, or API-key credentials), does not need stored tokens, and refuses cross-origin redirects, so the relay handles any upstream redirects. `--account` still selects the account label. Use https for endpoints that are not on loopback. Discovery documents still use `GOG_DISCOVERY_BASE_URL`; gRPC clients such as the Pub/Sub pull used by `gmail watch pull`, Maps/Places API-key calls, and downloads from non-googleapis.com URLs are not redirected, and `gog auth` commands still talk to Google directly. Invalid values fail with a usage error. Consumer Google accounts work with user-facing APIs. Admin Directory, Cloud Identity Groups, Chat, Keep, and domain-wide delegation require a managed Google Workspace domain. The [Workspace Admin guide](docs/workspace-admin.md) explains that setup. ## Automate safely `--json` emits structured output and `--plain` emits stable TSV. Prompts, progress, and warnings go to stderr. `--no-input`, `--readonly`, exact command allowlists, Gmail no-send policy, dry-run plans, and untrusted-content wrapping let the caller define a narrower execution boundary. ```bash gog --account you@gmail.com \ --enable-commands-exact gmail.search,gmail.get \ --gmail-no-send --readonly --no-input --wrap-untrusted --json \ gmail search 'newer_than:7d' ``` See [Automation](docs/automation.md) for output and exit-code contracts, and [Safety Profiles](docs/safety-profiles.md) for binaries with command policy and locked flag values baked in at build time. ## Accounts and authentication One installation can route among multiple Google accounts, named OAuth client projects, direct access tokens, Application Default Credentials, and Workspace service accounts. Tokens use the platform keyring by default; headless systems can use the encrypted file backend. ```bash gog auth list --check gog auth alias set work you@company.com gog --account work gmail search 'is:unread' ``` See [OAuth clients](docs/auth-clients.md) for client selection and service accounts, and [Paths and State](docs/paths.md) for `GOG_HOME`, XDG paths, and keyring storage. ## Discover the contract Running `gog` with no arguments shows the executable path, a short description, and local auth/config status. Use `gog --help` for the command overview. When JSON output is selected through the environment, the no-args view emits only the status JSON object. The running binary generates its command schema, reference pages, and agent skills from the same command tree: ```bash gog schema --json gog schema gmail search --json gog help drive inventory ``` `gog mcp` exposes a typed stdio MCP server without a generic shell or command bridge. It is read-only by default; writes require explicit command and tool authorization. See the [MCP guide](docs/mcp.md). ## Supported OAuth services The generated table below records the user OAuth and Workspace service-account surface. `gog auth services` reports the same information from the installed binary. The default `user`/`all-user` set excludes `ads`. Google treats authorizing an app for Google Ads as a sensitive action and can block consent behind a mandatory passkey enrollment. readmeHtml:
gog 🧭 — Google Workspace from the terminal

gog is one command-line client for Gmail, Calendar, Drive, Docs, Sheets, and the wider Google Workspace surface. It is built for people, scripts, CI, and agents that need explicit account routing, machine-readable output, and safety controls.

gog --readonly gmail search 'is:unread newer_than:7d' --max 10 --json
gog --readonly calendar events --today --json
gog --readonly drive audit sharing --parent <folderId> --json

For least-privilege Gmail authorization, use gog auth add you@example.com --services gmail --gmail-scope send for sending only, or --gmail-scope read-send to also read messages without mailbox-modification or settings-management permissions.

Install

Homebrew is the shortest path on macOS and Linux. Prebuilt macOS binaries require macOS 15 or later:

brew install openclaw/tap/gogcli
gog --version

With Go:

go install github.com/openclaw/gogcli/cmd/gog@latest
gog --version

Install scripts using the former github.com/steipete/gogcli module path should switch to github.com/openclaw/gogcli as shown above.

Docker images, Windows archives, raw macOS/Linux binaries, and source builds are covered in the install guide.

Quick start

Create a Desktop OAuth client in a Google Cloud project, download its JSON file, and authorize only the services you need:

gog auth credentials set ~/Downloads/client_secret_*.json
gog auth add you@gmail.com --services gmail,calendar,drive
export GOG_ACCOUNT=you@gmail.com
gog auth doctor --check
gog gmail search 'newer_than:7d' --max 10

gog auth you@gmail.com is shorthand for gog auth add you@gmail.com, with the same flags.

For Gmail queries beginning with -, place all flags before --; see Search and Read.

The five-minute quickstart covers API enablement, the OAuth consent screen, weekly-token-expiry avoidance, headless authorization, and account defaults.

Work with Google services

Commands follow the resource you are working with. These are the common entry points; the examples and generated command index cover the full surface.

Work Start with
Mail and calendars gog gmail search, gog calendar events
Files and sharing gog drive ls, gog drive audit sharing
Docs, Sheets, Slides, and Forms gog docs, gog sheets, gog slides, gog forms
Contacts and tasks gog contacts, gog tasks
Meetings and chat gog meet, gog chat, gog zoom
Analytics and publishing gog analytics, gog searchconsole, gog adsense, gog youtube
Workspace administration gog admin, gog groups, gog keep
Discovery API fallback gog api describe, gog api call

Generic API commands support service-hosted Discovery documents such as Meet v2 when the default central Directory returns 404. Explicit GOG_DISCOVERY_BASE_URL overrides retain their existing behavior.

GOG_GOOGLE_API_BASE_URL=http(s)://host[:port] sends Google API requests for https://googleapis.com and https://*.googleapis.com to a test server, emulator, proxy, or relay that adds credentials outside gog. Path and query are kept and the original host is sent as X-Forwarded-Host. While it is set, gog attaches no credentials to Google API requests (no OAuth, ADC, service-account, --access-token, or API-key credentials), does not need stored tokens, and refuses cross-origin redirects, so the relay handles any upstream redirects. --account still selects the account label. Use https for endpoints that are not on loopback. Discovery documents still use GOG_DISCOVERY_BASE_URL; gRPC clients such as the Pub/Sub pull used by gmail watch pull, Maps/Places API-key calls, and downloads from non-googleapis.com URLs are not redirected, and gog auth commands still talk to Google directly. Invalid values fail with a usage error.

Consumer Google accounts work with user-facing APIs. Admin Directory, Cloud Identity Groups, Chat, Keep, and domain-wide delegation require a managed Google Workspace domain. The Workspace Admin guide explains that setup.

Automate safely

--json emits structured output and --plain emits stable TSV. Prompts, progress, and warnings go to stderr. --no-input, --readonly, exact command allowlists, Gmail no-send policy, dry-run plans, and untrusted-content wrapping let the caller define a narrower execution boundary.

gog --account you@gmail.com \
  --enable-commands-exact gmail.search,gmail.get \
  --gmail-no-send --readonly --no-input --wrap-untrusted --json \
  gmail search 'newer_than:7d'

See Automation for output and exit-code contracts, and Safety Profiles for binaries with command policy and locked flag values baked in at build time.

Accounts and authentication

One installation can route among multiple Google accounts, named OAuth client projects, direct access tokens, Application Default Credentials, and Workspace service accounts. Tokens use the platform keyring by default; headless systems can use the encrypted file backend.

gog auth list --check
gog auth alias set work you@company.com
gog --account work gmail search 'is:unread'

See OAuth clients for client selection and service accounts, and Paths and State for GOG_HOME, XDG paths, and keyring storage.

Discover the contract

Running gog with no arguments shows the executable path, a short description, and local auth/config status. Use gog --help for the command overview. When JSON output is selected through the environment, the no-args view emits only the status JSON object.

The running binary generates its command schema, reference pages, and agent skills from the same command tree:

gog schema --json
gog schema gmail search --json
gog help drive inventory

gog mcp exposes a typed stdio MCP server without a generic shell or command bridge. It is read-only by default; writes require explicit command and tool authorization. See the MCP guide.

Supported OAuth services

The generated table below records the user OAuth and Workspace service-account surface. gog auth services reports the same information from the installed binary.

The default user/all-user set excludes ads. Google treats authorizing an app for Google Ads as a sensitive action and can block consent behind a mandatory passkey enrollment. Add it only when you need it: gog auth add you@example.com --services user,ads.

https://www.googleapis.com/auth/meetings.space.readonly
https://www.googleapis.com/auth/meetings.space.settings

https://www.googleapis.com/auth/script.deployments
https://www.googleapis.com/auth/script.processes
analytics yes Analytics Admin API, Analytics Data API https://www.googleapis.com/auth/analytics.readonly GA4 account summaries + reporting

https://www.googleapis.com/auth/admin.directory.group
https://www.googleapis.com/auth/admin.directory.group.member		 Workspace only; service account with domain-wide delegation required
youtube yes YouTube Data API v3 https://www.googleapis.com/auth/youtube.readonly Most read operations also work with API key only (config youtube_api_key or GOG_YOUTUBE_API_KEY)

photospicker no Photos Picker API https://www.googleapis.com/auth/photospicker.mediaitems.readonly Consumer OAuth; explicit opt-in with --services photospicker; selected media only

Documentation

gog drive get <fileId> --fields id,trashed --json preserves "trashed": false. The default metadata also includes false starred and hasThumbnail values. Conditionally absent fields (shared, ownedByMe, writersCanShare, and hasAugmentedPermissions) and nested booleans retain the SDK's omission behavior; use gog drive raw when you need the exact API response.

  • Overview and guides
  • Examples
  • Command index
  • Gmail workflows
  • Drive audits
  • AdSense accounts and reports
  • Docs, Sheets, and Slides guides
  • Changelog

gog is open source and is not affiliated with Google.

Credits

Inspired by Mario Zechner's gmcli, gccli, and gdcli.

Development

The project requires the Go version declared in go.mod.

make build
make test
make ci

See live testing for opt-in Google API smoke tests and releasing for the maintainer workflow.

License

MIT

releases.name: v0.48.0
releases.body:
## 0.48.0 - 2026-11-05

**Highlights:** New backups stay local until you configure a remote; existing configurations keep working. Store service-account keys in the keyring, search Gmail IDs efficiently, and use environment-backed watch tokens, with Calendar fixes and security dependency updates.

The backup changes in #1303 and #1304 preserve existing saved remotes and Git origins. Gmail attachment behavior after delivery (#1300) is contributor-reported; local MIME regression tests pass. Automatic reauthorization (#1278) has synthetic regression coverage but was not tested with a live consent flow.

- Backup: keep new backups local until a remote is configured; preserve saved remotes and existing Git origins, and explain local-only operation. (#1287) — thanks @NasAndNora.

- Backup: allow a locally initialized backup to acquire its first configured remote without replacing an existing origin. (#1287) — thanks @NasAndNora.

- Auth: add optional `auth service-account set --keyring` storage with migration back to files, isolated configuration references, and cleanup on rotation or unset; existing key files remain supported. (#1294) — thanks @tommyjoseph.

- Gmail: give every outgoing

releases.name: v0.47.1
releases.body:
## 0.47.1 - 2026-10-26

**Highlights:** Preserve Gmail text direction and narrowed Calendar grants, fix headless Linux authentication, and reject compromised certificates in the tracking worker.

- Gmail: give the author's own text its direction in HTML (`dir="auto"` on each line of converted plain text, once around given HTML, and on the signature) so right-to-left text reads correctly and English keeps its direction when a right-to-left reply quotes it; whole HTML documents go in as given. (#1255) — thanks @malob.

- Auth: use the encrypted file backend on headless Linux when D-Bus is explicitly disabled, instead of falling through to an uninitialized password store. (#1258) — thanks @pkyIntelligence.

- Auth: preserve Calendar read-only scope selections during automatic reauthorization instead of requesting previously granted broader access. (#1259) — thanks @pkyIntelligence.

- Security: update the tracking worker's workerd runtime to reject compromised eMudhra certificate chains. (#1264) — thanks @joshavant.

- Dependencies: update Google IAM, GAX, enterprise certificate support, Workers types, Wrangler, and oxlint-tsgolint while retaining Go 1.26 and the tracking worker’s 24-

releases.name: v0.47.0
releases.body:
## 0.47.0 - 2026-10-23

**Highlights:** Opt-in HTML Gmail bodies, selected search headers, and calendar settings updates, with OAuth error redaction and certificate trust fixes.

- Gmail: add opt-in `--html-from-text` (or `GOG_GMAIL_HTML_FROM_TEXT`) to generate an escaped HTML alternative for plain send, reply, and draft bodies; preserve plain-text defaults and explicit HTML. (#1251) — thanks @mathieu-ships.
- Gmail: expose up to 50 selected headers in message-search JSON and MCP with `--headers`, reusing existing reads and preserving sanitization and untrusted-content wrapping. (#1190, #1249) — thanks @obokaman-com.
- Calendar: add `update-calendar` to inspect or patch calendar-level names, descriptions, locations, and timezones, with field validation, offline previews, and explicit optional-field clearing. (#1245) — thanks @sorenisanerd.
- Auth: omit OAuth provider descriptions, URLs, and response bodies from command errors, per-item results, backup diagnostics, health checks, and watch/verbose logs; retain fixed recovery guidance, authentication exit codes, and both Calendar/Zoom rollback causes. (#1243) — thanks @pkyIntelligence.
- Security: upgrade Alpine's default CA packages

releases.name: v0.46.0
releases.body:
## 0.46.0 - 2026-10-20

**Highlights:** Safely re-encrypt auth stores, route Google API calls through credential-free relays, and compose richer Gmail forwards, with Go security fixes.

- Auth: add `gog auth rekey <outdir>` to write and verify a separate re-encrypted directory while leaving the live keyring untouched; hold the store lock throughout, publish only complete fsynced output, and retain the old directory during installation. (#1224) — thanks @sorenisanerd.
- Google APIs: add `GOG_GOOGLE_API_BASE_URL` to send `*.googleapis.com` requests to a test server, emulator, proxy, or relay that adds credentials outside gog; requests keep path and query, pass the original host as `X-Forwarded-Host`, carry no gog credentials, and refuse cross-origin redirects. (#1225, #1226) — thanks @km-tr.
- Gmail: add `--note-html` and `--note-html-file` to forwards and preserve plain-note line breaks in HTML output. (#1215) — thanks @malob.
- Auth: accept `gog auth <email>` as shorthand for `gog auth add <email>`; bare `gog auth` and mistyped subcommands keep their existing errors. (#1221)
- Gmail: lay out the forwarded-message header block the way Gmail Web does: plain text with the sender's nam

releases.name: v0.45.0
releases.body:
## 0.45.0 - 2026-10-16

**Highlights:** Preserve Gmail search results for negated and OR queries, warn about unmatched JSON selections, and improve reply formatting.

- Gmail: derive `labelIds` only from system-label terms that hold for every result; a term under `NOT` or `-`, inside a negated group, or in a query with `OR`, `|` or `{…}` is left to Gmail, so `search`, `--count`, `archive`, `trash`, `mark-read`, `unread` and `autoreply` no longer silently narrow such queries. (#1212) — thanks @wstock.
- Output: warn on stderr when a `--select` path matches no objects in a nonempty result, preserving JSON output and exit status. (#1210) — thanks @postoso.
- Gmail: render the reply attribution line the way Gmail Web does in both text and HTML: no comma after the date, `Name <email>` (or `<email>`) with the address linked in HTML, and a narrow no-break space before AM/PM (also in forwarded `Date:` lines). (#1213) — thanks @malob.
- Auth: clarify that `auth login` opens the browser account manager, and document manual authorization and unattended health checks. (#1214) — thanks @jingtying.
- Dependencies: refresh Google API and MCP clients plus tracking-worker tooling within the Go 1.26

aiSummary.oneLiner: A unified, task-first CLI for automating Google Workspace operations.
aiSummary.whatItDoes: gog consolidates the sprawling Google Workspace APIs into a single CLI binary designed for both human operators and automated scripts. It provides task-first commands that abstract away the complexity of raw REST resources, enabling practical workflows like auditing Drive sharing, sending Gmail, resolving calendar names, editing Docs, and managing Workspace users. It enforces strict operational contracts to make automation reliable, offering stable JSON output for CI environments, comprehensive exit codes, and robust read-only flags to prevent accidental modifications. It essentially turns Google Workspace into a scriptable command-line toolkit.
keyFeatures: Unified Workspace access: Manages Gmail, Calendar, Drive, Docs, Admin, and over a dozen other Google services from a single binary.
Task-oriented abstraction: Replaces raw API calls with practical workflows like finding unread mail or auditing folder permissions.
Automation-ready output: Supports `--json` and `--plain` stdout for script parsing, while strictly routing warnings and prompts to stderr.
Safety guardrails: Includes `--readonly`, `--gmail-no-send`, and `--no-input` flags for secure, non-interactive CI execution.
Flexible authentication: Supports account aliases, OAuth clients, direct access tokens, OS keyrings, and Workspace service accounts.

useCases.title: CI/CD reporting
useCases.description: Runs non-interactively in a CI pipeline to parse test results and append them directly to a Google Sheet.

useCases.title: Security auditing
useCases.description: Executes read-only queries to dump Drive folder sharing permissions to a JSON file for scheduled compliance reviews.

useCases.title: Agent tool integration
useCases.description: Provides autonomous coding agents with a predictable, CLI-based tool to safely interact with a user's calendar or email.

useCases.title: Workspace administration
useCases.description: Use bulk commands to manage Workspace users, update group memberships, and back up account data via the terminal.

aiSummary.whoIsItFor: DevOps engineers, IT admins, and developers needing a scriptable, predictable interface to manage and automate Google Workspace. Ideal for teams requiring efficient go.
